samples.text:
The line graph shows how many people visited a museum every year from 2016 to 2024, and the table shows where the museum got its money from in 2016 and 2024.

In 2016 the museum had 610 thousand visitors and the number increased every year until 2019, when it was 720 thousand. However, in 2020 the visitors fell sharply to only 150 thousand. After that the number went up again, it was 280 thousand in 2021, 530 thousand in 2022 and 680 thousand in 2023. In 2024 there were 760 thousand visitors, the highest number.

Looking at the table, the government grant was the biggest source of income in 2016 with $6.2 million, but it decreased to $4.1 million in 2024. On the other hand, ticket sales increased from $2.4 million to $4.6 million and it became the biggest source. The shop and café income also increased from $1.3 million to $2.5 million and donations went up from $0.8 million to $1.1 million. The total rised from $10.7 million to $12.3 million.

Overall, the visitors recovered after 2020 and the museum got less money from government but more from tickets.
samples.why: Brief overview placed at the end · all figures accurate, both visuals covered · repetitive linking and verbs (increased, went up) · errors in verb forms, pronoun agreement, articles and a comma splice.

samples.text:
The line graph shows the number of people who visited a museum annually between 2016 and 2024, and the table compares the museum's income from four sources in 2016 and 2024.

Overall, visitor numbers grew steadily except for a dramatic fall in 2020, after which they recovered to a new high. Meanwhile, the museum's total income increased, with ticket sales replacing the government grant as its main source of money.

In 2016, 610 thousand people visited the museum, and this rose each year to 720 thousand in 2019. In 2020, however, visitor numbers collapsed to only 150 thousand, around a fifth of the previous year's figure. A strong recovery followed, with numbers climbing to 530 thousand in 2022 and to 760 thousand in 2024, which exceeded the pre-2020 peak.

Regarding income, the government grant fell from US$6.2 million to US$4.1 million, while income from ticket sales almost doubled, from US$2.4 million to US$4.6 million, making it the largest source by 2024. Earnings from the shop and café also nearly doubled to US$2.5 million, and donations rises slightly from US$0.8 million to US$1.1 million. As a result, the museum's total income increased from US$10.7 million to US$12.3 million.
samples.why: Clear overview linking visitors and income · key features highlighted with accurate comparisons (a fifth, almost doubled) · good cohesion · some less common vocabulary (collapsed, exceeded) · one minor agreement slip.

samples.text:
The line graph charts annual visitor numbers at a museum from 2016 to 2024, while the table sets out the museum's income by source in the first and last of those years.

Apart from a severe slump in 2020, attendance rose throughout the period, ending at its highest level. Over the same timeframe, the museum's income grew and its funding shifted markedly away from government support towards earned revenue, particularly ticket sales.

Visitor numbers increased steadily from 610 thousand in 2016 to 720 thousand in 2019, before plunging to just 150 thousand in 2020, only around a fifth of the previous year's total. The recovery was rapid: attendance almost doubled to 280 thousand in 2021, reached 680 thousand in 2023, and hit a high of 760 thousand in 2024.

In 2016, the government grant of US$6.2 million made up well over half of the museum's US$10.7 million income. By 2024, however, the grant had been cut to US$4.1 million and was overtaken by ticket sales, which nearly doubled from US$2.4 million to US$4.6 million. Revenue from the shop and café rose by a similar proportion, from US$1.3 million to US$2.5 million, and donations edged up from US$0.8 million to US$1.1 million. As a result, total income reached US$12.3 million.
samples.why: Skilful overview connecting attendance and funding · figures selected purposefully with accurate proportions · cohesion managed smoothly · precise vocabulary (slump, earned revenue, edged up) · wide range of error-free structures.
